exposure: COVID-19 severity classification (asymptomatic, mild, severe pneumonia)
cohort: The study included 247 hospitalized pregnant women with a positive RT-PCR and/or rapid test for SARS-CoV-2 in the second half of pregnancy at Edgardo Rebagliati Martins National Hospital from March to July 2020.
finding: The possibility of cesarean section and iatrogenic preterm delivery is greater in severe COVID-19 cases, while the vaginal delivery rate increased in recent months, and no perinatal complications directly related to COVID-19 were identified.
mod_finding: The overall cesarean section rate was high at 60%, increasing to 100% in severe cases, although the rate of vaginal deliveries doubled over the study period.
gest_age: Babies born from pregnancies ≥20 weeks gestation
